Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-02, batch 40 (Equinix missing-address campaign): added a two source agreeing aggregator address, noted Herndon sits within Fairfax County so this is not a conflict with the registrys existing city field, research_status remains complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Equinix operates a very large global portfolio and this session found its own per-building pages under equinix.com/data-centers/ to be inconsistently populated: some individual IBX codes 404 entirely (confirmed fresh this session for DC17), and others that do load, such as DC7, checked fresh this session, still omit street address and square footage, deferring that detail to a downloadable specification sheet not reachable by this research pass. Given this, addresses in this batch rely on aggregator sourcing, preferring cases with independent multi source agreement, per this registrys standard source hierarchy. This specific row, DC97, per registry coordinates in Fairfax County, VA. A prior research pass found the operators own DC97 page 404ing and treated a third party Herndon, VA lead as unconfirmed. This session finds two independent aggregators, Inflect and DataCenterMap, agreeing exactly on 460 Spring Park Pl (also rendered Springpark Place), Herndon, VA. Herndon is itself an incorporated town within Fairfax County, so this address is consistent with, not contradictory to, the registrys own Fairfax County city field.

reading.body:
Equinix DC97 is a colocation facility in Herndon, within the Washington DC metro region's 15-facility complex that Equinix positions as North America's largest peering point. The operator publishes no power capacity, floor area, or investment figure for this individual building, and the facility's own specification page is not currently accessible. It sits within Virginia's published data center capacity of 1,375 megawatts across 23 mapped facilities, a ranking below the state's disclosed figures.

The DC metro region as a whole serves as a major communications gateway to Europe and benefits from proximity to federal infrastructure demand. Culpeper County has recently emerged as a newer extension of the Ashburn corridor, suggesting capacity expansion beyond the original cluster. However, without published specifications for DC97 itself, its specific role in that regional footprint and its contribution to either AI training density or edge compute cannot be determined from available data.

For a reader assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the absence of published capacity data is the binding constraint. The facility exists as part of a strategically positioned peering complex, but its power envelope, rack count, and thermal capability are not disclosed by the operator, making any assessment of its relevance to AI workloads speculative rather than fact-based.
